subject.title: California — Proposition 2 (Increases State's Rainy Day Fund)

positions.statement: CADC supports Prop. 2 because setting aside more revenue during strong economic years can help California withstand future downturns without imposing a new tax.

subject.title: California — Proposition 3 (Provides Permanent Funding for Schools and Health Care by Extending Existing Tax on High Incomes)

positions.statement: CADC supports Prop. 3 because these rates have been in place for many years and generate substantial funding for schools and other public services; allowing them to expire could result in a significant revenue loss.

subject.title: California — Proposition 4 (Repeals Prohibition Against Public Funding of Election Campaigns)

positions.statement: CADC supports Prop. 4 because public financing can reduce candidates' dependence on wealthy donors and special interests, and San Francisco already has experience with such a system.

subject.title: California — Proposition 5 (Changes Recall Election Process for Statewide Officers)

positions.statement: CADC supports Prop. 5 because the existing process can allow a replacement candidate with substantially less than majority support to take office and can turn recalls into partisan alternative elections.

subject.title: California — Proposition 37 (Creates Loan Program for Middle-Income Buyers of Qualified New Homes)

positions.statement: CADC supports Prop. 37 because it can expand homeownership for middle-income families while encouraging construction of additional housing.

subject.title: California — Proposition 38 (Authorizes Bonds for Immunology Medical Research)

positions.statement: CADC recognizes the importance of medical research but opposes Prop. 38 because the state would incur approximately $500 million annually in debt service for about 25 years while the financial and medical returns remain uncertain.

subject.title: California — Proposition 39 (Prohibits Citizens from Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification)

positions.statement: CADC opposes Prop. 39 because citizenship is already required to vote and California already uses voter-registration and signature-verification systems.

subject.title: California — Proposition 40 (Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers)

positions.statement: CADC opposes Prop. 40 because taxing unrealized wealth and difficult-to-value assets could be administratively complicated and could encourage high-income residents and entrepreneurs to relocate, potentially reducing California's future income-tax base.

subject.title: California — Proposition 41 (Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes)

positions.statement: CADC supports Prop. 41 because new taxes should remain subject to established spending controls and accountability requirements.

subject.title: California — Proposition 42 (Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes)

positions.statement: CADC supports Prop. 42 because it establishes a constitutional limit against new wealth or asset taxes and retroactive taxation.

subject.title: California — Proposition 43 (Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services)

positions.statement: CADC opposes Prop. 43 because it would make it substantially harder for local communities to approve taxes for services they choose to fund.

subject.title: California — Proposition 44 (Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% Of Revenue on Program Services)

positions.statement: CADC opposes Prop. 44 because members questioned whether a rigid statewide 90% requirement adequately accounts for administrative and operational costs.

subject.title: California — Proposition 45 (Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects)

positions.statement: CADC opposes Prop. 45 because the committee was concerned that accelerating review and restricting alternatives could weaken meaningful environmental protections.

subject.title: Bay Area — Regional Measure RTM (Regional Transit Measure)

positions.statement: CADC supports RTM because public transit needs stable funding to maintain essential service, therefore, a broadly based sales tax spreads the cost across the general population, and is more equitable than Prop H which primarily place the transit-funding burden on property owners.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition A (Charter Changes Affecting Various City Departments and Commissions)

positions.statement: CADC supports Prop. A because San Francisco has accumulated numerous overlapping, inactive or duplicative bodies that can diffuse responsibility and consume staff resources.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition B (Establishing a Municipal Finance Corporation and a Public Bank)

positions.statement: CADC opposes Prop. B because the measure creates the institutional framework without identifying a secure source for the substantial capitalization needed to establish the bank.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition D (Changes to Ballot Measure Process)

positions.statement: CADC opposes Prop. D because it would effectively eliminate grassroots volunteer signature-gathering as a practical path to the ballot, leaving well-funded campaigns better able to qualify measures by paying professional petition circulators—currently around $18 per signature.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition E (City Administrator's Authority and Changes to City Contracting)

positions.statement: CADC supports Prop. E because members believe San Francisco's contracting and procurement system can be unnecessarily slow and fragmented and that clearer centralized responsibility can improve efficiency and accountability.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition F (Changes to Executive Branch Management)

positions.statement: Having already supported Prop. A to streamline commissions and Prop. E to expand the City Administrator's authority and streamline contracting, CADC believes Prop. F goes a step too far by further reducing existing checks and balances.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition G (Allowing Private Vehicles on the Great Highway in Sunset Dunes Park)

positions.statement: CADC supports Prop. G as a balanced approach that preserves the corridor for recreation while restoring weekday transportation access for working families, seniors, people with disabilities and others who rely on vehicles.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition H (Parcel Tax to Fund Public Muni Operations)

positions.statement: CADC opposes Prop. H because San Francisco voters are simultaneously being asked to approve a regional transit sales tax that would also provide substantial new funding to Muni.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition I (Changes to Real Property Transfer Tax)

positions.statement: CADC opposes Prop. I because the measure would restrict future use of volatile transfer-tax revenue and reduce the City's flexibility to respond to changing budget needs.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition J (Removal of Foreclosure Exemption for Real Property Transfer Tax)

positions.statement: CADC supports Prop. J because the majority concluded that large lenders and investors taking ownership of major properties should not automatically receive a transfer-tax exemption unavailable in an ordinary sale and that such properties should contribute to City revenues.
